PHASE 1Batch drum roaster, 10-25 kg, electric, PID + grain-bed thermocouple
S07 Roasting		Horizontal rotating SS304 drum, 10-25 kg per batch; electric heating (or LPG); digital PID with a thermocouple placed IN THE GRAIN BED, not just on the drum wall; variable drum speed 5-20 rpm; manual tilt or slide discharge; insulated body; interlocked door85,000 – 180,000Roasting is the step that converts a 6-week product into a 6-9 month product, and it is your main flavour differentiator. Electric over LPG: LPG is ~30% cheaper to run but the temperature control is far worse, and inconsistent roasting costs you far more in rejected batches than the electricity saves. For a quality-first, low-labour unit, buy electric with a PID.Weekly: brush and wipe the drum interior, check the drum drive chain/belt and the support rollers, clean the discharge chute. Monthly: CALIBRATE the thermocouple against an independent dial or IR thermometer - drift of 10-15 C is common and invisible; inspect the heating elements and contactors; check the door interlock. Keep spares: 1 thermocouple (Rs 800-2,500), 1 heating element, 1 contactor, 1 SSR.
PHASE 1SS304 impact pulveriser / micro-pulveriser with cyclone + bag filter (PRIMARY MILL)
S09 Grinding		5-7.5 HP (3.7-5.6 kW), three-phase; output 30-80 kg/h on millet flour; air-swept design with a cyclone and a cloth filter bag; interchangeable screens 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 mesh; ALL contact parts SS304; accessible chamber for cleaning; overload protection; hopper with a slide gate for controlled feeding90,000 – 250,000This is your production workhorse - 6 of your 10 SKUs depend on it. Buy SS304 contact parts (a mild-steel pulveriser is fine for spices, not acceptable for a premium food brand) and an AIR-SWEPT design so the blower carries the flour out: that keeps the flour 10-15 C cooler than a gravity-discharge mill, which directly improves shelf life. Interchangeable screens let one machine make 60-mesh ragi, 80-mesh sprouted flour and 40-mesh dosa mix.DAILY: brush out the chamber, cyclone and pipe; remove and wash the screen; check the filter bag for dust leakage (a leaking bag is silently sending your finest flour into the air); inspect the beaters for wear and the screen for holes; check the magnet in the discharge chute. WEEKLY: check belt tension and alignment, listen for bearing noise, grease per schedule, inspect the door gaskets. MONTHLY: check motor amp draw against nameplate, tighten all fasteners, inspect electrical connections for heat discolouration. SPARES TO KEEP ON THE SHELF: 2 screens (60 and 80 mesh), 1 beater set, 2 filter bags, 1 belt set. Total ~Rs 12,000 - and it turns a 5-day breakdown into a 20-minute fix.
PHASE 1Stone chakki / stone flour mill, 2-3 HP (SECONDARY + BACKUP)
S09 Grinding		2-3 HP, 40-60 kg/h; 12-18 inch emery/stone grinding discs; adjustable gap; SS or MS body with an SS flour outlet; single-phase preferred25,000 – 60,000Three reasons to own one even though the pulveriser does the job: (1) LOWER GRINDING TEMPERATURE - stone milling runs cooler, which is genuinely better for sprouted and high-fat flours; (2) MARKETING - 'stone-ground' is a real, defensible premium claim and lets you launch a separate SKU at a higher price; (3) BACKUP - if the pulveriser motor burns out you can still ship. At Rs 25-55k it is the cheapest insurance and the cheapest marketing you will buy.Every 150-250 running hours: DRESS (re-cut) the stone grooves with a dressing stone - an undressed stone polishes itself, stops cutting, and produces coarse flour while overheating the grain. This is the one maintenance task everyone forgets. Weekly: check the gap setting, clean the flour outlet and the stone housing, check belt tension. Spares: 1 spare stone pair (Rs 3,000-8,000), 1 dressing stone, belts.
PHASE 1Vibro sifter / powder screener, SS304, 24-30 inch
S10 Sifting		600-750 mm diameter single or double deck; SS304 contact parts; 0.5-1 HP vibration motor; 30-150 kg/h; quick-release clamp ring for screen changes; dust-tight lid; mesh 40 / 60 / 80 as required35,000 – 90,000Guarantees uniform particle size (the difference between 'premium' and 'gritty' in the customer's hand) AND - more importantly - its OVERS STREAM IS YOUR EARLY-WARNING SYSTEM. Whatever gets past your cleaning and grinding shows up in the sifter tailings. Inspecting that tailings tray every batch is free intelligence.Between products: remove the screen, brush both faces, vacuum the deck and - critically - the SKIRT SEALS, where flour hides and turns into insects. Weekly: inspect the screen for fatigue cracks and stretched mesh, check the rubber suspension balls/grommets, check the clamp ring torque. Monthly: check the vibration motor mounting and the electrical box for dust ingress.
PHASE 1Ribbon blender, 50 kg batch, SS304, reversible drive
S12 Blending		50 kg/batch (buy 50 kg, not 25 kg); SS304 U-trough; full-length double ribbon; 2-3 HP with a VFD for forward/reverse; flush-bottom discharge valve (not a slide gate that leaves a dead pocket); lid safety interlock; C-frame or legs at working height55,000 – 130,000Without it, your three ready mixes cannot be made consistently - hand-mixing 100 kg of 11 ingredients will never pass a uniformity test. The mixes are your highest-margin SKUs and they need exactly ONE new machine. That is the best ROI in this entire list.IMMEDIATELY after every batch (before residue sets): dry-brush, wash with food-grade detergent, rinse, sanitise, air-dry, and LEAVE THE LID OPEN so the chamber dries completely. A closed damp blender grows mould overnight. Weekly: inspect the ribbon ends and the discharge valve for trapped material, check the gasket, verify the interlock. Monthly: check the gearbox oil level, belt tension, and the VFD for dust (blow it out - flour dust kills VFD fans). Quarterly: check the ribbons for wear/bending - a bent ribbon leaves an unmixed core and you will not see it.
PHASE 1Platform scale 150 kg x 5 g + bench scale 30 kg x 1 g + certified weights
S11/S14 Weighing		Legal-for-trade (stamped) platform scale 150 kg x 5 g with a print or RS232 output; bench scale 30 kg x 1 g; a set of certified standard weights (500 g, 1 kg, 2 kg) for daily verification15,000 – 36,000Your entire legal compliance (net quantity) and your entire formulation accuracy (mixes) rest on these two scales. They are also the cheapest machines on this list. A scale with a PRINT output means the weight lands on the batch card automatically, which removes transcription errors and gives you an audit trail.DAILY (60 seconds): zero the scale, place the certified standard weight, confirm within +-1 g, record it in the calibration log. Weekly: clean under the platform (a grain of sand under the load cell changes the reading), check the cable for damage, confirm the level bubble is centred. Annually: get it re-verified and stamped by Legal Metrology.
PHASE 1Semi-automatic load-cell auger filler / weigh-filler, 10-2000 g
S14 Filling		SS304 contact hopper and auger; load-cell based gravimetric filling (not volumetric cups); range 10-2000 g; accuracy +-0.5-1%; foot-pedal trigger; coarse + dribble (fine) two-stage fill; 200-500 packs/h; a platform or table mount; product-level sensor in the hopper65,000 – 225,000At 250-500 packs a day, manual scooping-and-weighing is your throughput bottleneck AND your legal risk (under-weight packs) AND your margin leak (over-weight give-away). A load-cell filler fixes all three. It is the machine that pays for itself fastest after the destoner. Volumetric cup fillers are cheaper but they fill by VOLUME, and flour density changes with humidity and settling - so your weights drift all day. Insist on LOAD CELL (gravimetric).Daily: brush and vacuum the auger, hopper and nozzle; do NOT hose it down unless it is designed for wet cleaning (water in a load cell or a control box is the most common way these machines die). Verify accuracy with 5 test pouches. Weekly: inspect the auger for wear and burrs, check the load-cell mounting for looseness or obstruction (a loose mounting = drift), clean the level sensor. Monthly: calibrate with certified weights, check the foot-pedal switch and the wiring.
PHASE 1FR-900 continuous band sealer (SS body) + hand impulse sealer
S15 Sealing		FR-900 series, horizontal for 200-500 g pouches (and a vertical unit later for 1 kg bags); digital temperature control 0-300 C; adjustable belt speed 0-12 m/min; seal width 10-15 mm; optional embossing/printing wheel; optional counter; SS body preferred over MS11,000 – 45,000It is the cheapest machine in your plant, it is a GLOBAL STANDARD design (so spares - Teflon tape, heating element, silicone rubber, belt - are available in every city for a few hundred rupees), and it seals 400-900 packs per hour. This is the definition of the right first machine: low capital, low maintenance cost, universal spares, easy to learn.Daily: clean the belt and the sealing wheels with a soft brush and a damp cloth (powder residue causes poor seals and burnt film), check the Teflon tape for discolouration or tears, run the belt for 2 minutes with the heater off at the end of the shift so it does not set in a kink. Weekly: inspect the heating element and the silicone rubber strip for hardening or grooves, check the belt tracking, lubricate the gearbox per the manual. Monthly: verify the temperature display against an independent surface thermometer (a 15 C error = every seal weak or every seal melted).
PHASE 1Handheld TIJ thermal inkjet batch coder
S16 Coding		Handheld thermal inkjet (TIJ) printer, 12.7 mm or 25.4 mm print height; solvent/ethanol-based food-grade ink cartridges; prints date, batch, MRP, QR, barcode, text, logos; 3-6 hours battery; works on foil laminate, kraft, plastic, carton9,000 – 30,000For Rs 10-25k you get legible, indelible, professional batch coding on every pack. Batch coding is not cosmetic - it is what makes a one-batch recall possible instead of a brand-wide recall.Cap the printhead EVERY time you stop, even for 10 minutes (a dried TIJ head is often unrecoverable and the replacement is 60% of the machine's cost). Store the cartridge per the maker's instructions. Clean the head with the recommended solution only, never with a cloth that sheds lint. Keep the battery charged. Print a test strip at the start of every run.
PHASE 1QC instruments: moisture analyser, sieves, balance
S17 QC Lab		Halogen moisture analyser (0.01 g readability, 110-160 g capacity, 105/130 C programmes) | IS/ASTM test sieves 20/30/40/60/80/100 mesh with a mechanical sieve shaker | analytical balance 0.01 g | IR thermometer | chlorine test strips | thermo-hygrometers (3-4)45,000 – 130,000You cannot manage what you cannot measure, and you cannot defend a complaint without your own data. A moisture analyser and a sieve set cost less than one bad batch. This is the equipment that turns 'I think it is dry' into 'it is 8.4%'.Moisture analyser: clean the heating chamber and the sample pan holder after every test (residue changes the reading), replace pans (they are consumable), verify weekly against the oven method or a certified moisture standard. Sieves: brush both faces with a soft brush after every use, never tap them on a hard surface (it distorts the mesh), inspect monthly for mesh damage. Balance: keep it level, away from vibration and drafts, calibrate with certified weights daily.
PHASE 1Dehumidifier (packing + grinding + FG store) and AC
S08/S14/S18 Environment		Industrial/commercial desiccant or refrigerant dehumidifier, 24-50 L/day for a 200-400 sq ft packing room; plus a split AC 1.5-2 ton for the packing and germination rooms50,000 – 120,000This is the most UNDER-BOUGHT and most valuable item for a powder business in India. Flour packing above 60% RH means caking, clumping, poor flow, inaccurate filling, weak seals and short shelf life - and in the monsoon it will destroy your product. A dehumidified packing room is what separates a professional unit from a home kitchen. In most Indian cities it pays for itself in avoided rejects within 6 months.Fortnightly: clean or replace the air filter (a blocked filter halves the capacity). Monthly: clean the coil, check the condensate drain is not blocked, empty/verify the tank or confirm the continuous drain works. Quarterly: professional service. Keep the room closed - an open door defeats the machine.
PHASE 1Magnetic grate / rare-earth magnets (Phase 1); metal detector (Phase 2)
S13 Metal control		Phase 1: rare-earth (neodymium) magnetic grate or sleeved bar magnets, 10,000+ gauss, SS housing, fitted in the flour chute. Phase 2: gravity free-fall metal detector for powders or a small conveyor metal detector for sealed pouches, detecting Fe 1.5 mm / NFe 2.0 mm / SS 2.5 mm, with automatic reject and test-card verification3,000 – 15,000Phase 1 magnets are almost free and they catch exactly the contamination you are most likely to generate (ferrous particles from mill and screen wear) - which is also the kind most likely to injure a child. Fit them on day one. A metal detector becomes worth it when you supply modern-trade retail or quick-commerce, because their vendor audits demand documented metal detection with test-card records.Magnets: pull and inspect every 2 hours, wipe onto a white tissue, log what you find. Annually: verify the gauss rating with a gauss meter (magnets lose strength with heat and shock). Detector: daily cleaning, test cards every 2 h, annual manufacturer calibration.
PHASE 2Automatic VFFS pouch packing machine (form-fill-seal) - PHASE 2
S14/S15 Phase 2		Vertical form-fill-seal machine with a servo auger filler for powders; forms the pouch from printed roll stock; 20-60 pouches/min; filling range 100-1000 g; inline batch coder; photo-eye registration for printed film; SS304 contact parts380,000 – 900,000Buy this ONLY when you are consistently packing more than ~1,500-2,000 pouches/day of a small number of SKUs. Below that, a semi-auto filler plus a band sealer is cheaper, more flexible across 10 SKUs, and far easier to maintain. A VFFS machine also requires printed ROLL STOCK (higher MOQ, cylinder cost Rs 25,000-60,000 per colour) rather than pre-made pouches, which locks up working capital. This is the classic 'too-early automation' trap for a new brand.Daily cleaning of the forming tube, sealing jaws and auger; weekly jaw-face inspection and Teflon replacement; monthly pneumatic and sensor checks; annual AMC. Requires a trained technician - factor in one person becoming your VFFS expert.
PHASE 2Carton handling and dispatch aids - PHASE 2
S18/S19 Phase 2		Semi-automatic carton taping/sealing machine; barcode or QR scanner linked to a stock sheet; hand pallet truck; stretch-wrap dispenser25,000 – 180,000Not needed at 25-50 kg/day. At 150 kg/day a carton sealer and a scanner-linked FIFO system remove two full-time-equivalent hours a day and eliminate picking errors.Weekly cleaning and belt/roller inspection on the sealer; keep the scanner lens clean.
PHASE 1Facility and utility fit-out (not machines, but capital you must budget)
Facility		Epoxy or smooth-tiled flooring with coved skirting; washable walls; insect killers (2); air curtains or PVC strip curtains at external doors; mesh on all windows; hands-free handwash station; 3-sink wash area; changing room with lockers and a phone shelf; separate rooms for raw store / processing / sprouting / grinding / packing / FG store; three-phase electrical connection with proper earthing and an ELCB/RCCB; exhaust ventilation; water RO/UV treatment if the supply is not potable; adequate LED lighting (500 lux over work surfaces)250,000 – 600,000This is where first-time founders run out of money, because they budget for machines and not for the building. FSSAI licensing and Schedule 4 (Good Manufacturing Practices / GHP and GMP) requirements are mostly about the FACILITY: washable surfaces, no cross-contamination between raw and finished, handwash facilities, pest exclusion, adequate light and ventilation, and separate storage. Get the layout right ONCE - a bad flow cannot be fixed with paperwork.Monthly: check insect killers (replace glue boards/tubes), clean air-curtain filters, test the ELCB/RCCB trip button, check for leaks and roof damage, verify the RO/UV lamp hours and replace the lamp on schedule.
Phase-1 machinery sub-total: Rs 943,000 – Rs 2,481,000. Machinery is only ~30-35% of the true project cost; facility fit-out, packaging, compliance, working capital and contingency are the rest. See the budget section below.

Choose a printer who will (a) print a short digital run of 500-1,000 for your launch, (b) supply the film technical data sheet (laminate structure, total micron, seal-initiation temperature, WVTR and OTR values), and (c) hold blank stock so you can reorder in 3 days. The technical data sheet is what you give the sealer operator to set the temperature - ask for it.
Best for
All pouches and bags
Caution / insist on
Do NOT order 20,000 rotogravure pouches for a launch SKU you have not sold yet - that is the single most common way a new food brand locks up Rs 1.5-3 lakh in packaging it cannot use. Start with digital-print short runs or blank pouches + labels, prove the SKU for 3 months, then commit to cylinders. Also: verify the laminate is FOOD-GRADE and ask for a migration/compliance declaration, and check the WVTR - for a 9-month flour shelf life you want a foil (AL) layer, not just metallised polyester.
Confidence
Market rates verified from IndiaMART listings and vendor sites, Sep-2026. Get 3 quotes
NABL / FSSAI-notified food testing laboratories  | Pan-India | Everything in the QC and compliance plan…
Relevant products
Microbiological testing (TPC, yeast & mould, coliform, E. coli, Salmonella, B. cereus), nutritional analysis for the label panel, heavy metals, pesticide residues, aflatoxin, peroxide value / free fatty acid for shelf life, moisture and ash, gluten ELISA, accelerated shelf-life studies
Phone
Use the FSSAI notified-lab list and the NABL directory (nabl-india.org -> 'Search Accredited Laboratories'). National chains with food labs: SGS India, Bureau Veritas India, Intertek, Eurofins, TUV SUD South Asia, Thermo Fisher / ALS. Government institutes: CFTRI Mysore, NIFTEM Sonipat, IIFPT Thanjavur, and your State Food Testing Laboratory. For millets specifically, also check the APEDA-recognised laboratory list (itrack.apeda.gov.in) - it explicitly covers 'pesticides and heavy metals in food products including cereals, grains, pulses and MILLETS'.
Email
via each lab's website
Website
fssai.gov.in (notified labs) | nabl-india.org | itrack.apeda.gov.in
Address / contact person
Pan-India; choose one within courier distance and one national chain as a cross-check
Hours
Sample drop-off windows vary
Price examples
Routine microbiology Rs 2,000-5,000 per sample | full nutritional panel for a label Rs 6,000-12,000 per SKU (one time) | heavy metals Rs 2,500-5,000 | pesticide residue multi-residue screen Rs 6,000-15,000 | aflatoxin Rs 1,500-3,500 | peroxide value / FFA Rs 800-2,000 | moisture, ash, particle size Rs 300-1,200 each
Service & maintenance
Pick a lab that (a) is NABL ISO/IEC 17025 accredited FOR THE SPECIFIC TESTS you need (check the scope, not just the certificate), (b) is FSSAI-notified, (c) gives a turnaround of 3-7 working days, and (d) will courier a sample kit to you. Government labs (CFTRI, NIFTEM, IIFPT, state labs) are cheaper and authoritative but slower; private chains are faster and costlier. A practical setup: one private chain for routine monthly micro, and CFTRI/NIFTEM for your one-time label nutrition panel and for any dispute.
Best for
Everything in the QC and compliance plan
Caution / insist on
Budget for testing in your cost sheet - it is a real recurring cost, not an optional extra. Do not use a lab that is not accredited for the specific test; an unaccredited report is worthless in a regulatory dispute. Send samples in insulated packaging with a cold chain for microbiology.
Confidence
Accreditation route and indicative costs verified from NABL/FSSAI/APEDA sources and lab websites, Sep-2026

Subsidies, grants and funding

PMFME - Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (MoFPI)
Benefit
Credit-linked capital subsidy of 35% of the eligible project cost, ceiling Rs 10.0 lakh per individual micro unit. Additional support for SHG members, FPOs and common infrastructure. 50% grant for branding & marketing to FPO/SHG/cooperative groups or an SPV of micro enterprises. Seed capital of Rs 40,000 per SHG member for working capital and small tools.
Status / urgency
*** ACT IMMEDIATELY *** The scheme runs 2020-21 to 2025-26 and the current deadline is 30 September 2026 - FOUR DAYS from today (26 Sep 2026). It has already achieved its 2 lakh-unit target and an extension beyond 30 Sep 2026 with revised norms has been publicly proposed/announced as likely, but that is not something you can rely on. ACTION TODAY: call your District PMFME Resource Person (DRP) or the District Agriculture/Industry office and ask whether applications are still being accepted, and simultaneously prepare your DPR so you can file on the day any extension is notified.
How to apply
Apply through your bank (it is CREDIT-LINKED - you take a term loan and the subsidy is released against it). You need: a Detailed Project Report (DPR), quotation-based machine list, FSSAI registration/licence, GST, Udyam registration, land/lease proof, and the bank's sanction. The State Nodal Agency and the District Resource Person help you free of cost. Portal: pmfme.mofpi.gov.in. Guidelines PDF: mofpi.gov.in.
Fit for you
EXCELLENT FIT for you. A Rs 20-30 lakh Phase-1 project could attract up to Rs 10 lakh of subsidy, i.e. roughly 33-50% of your machinery cost. Millets are an explicitly prioritised category under PMFME, and many states have additional top-ups.
Contact / where
pmfme.mofpi.gov.in | Your State Nodal Agency (listed on the portal) | your District Resource Person (DRP) | your bank's MSME/Priority Sector branch | MoFPI helpline via the portal
State millet / horticulture and food-processing missions
Benefit
Varies by state: 25-50% capital subsidy on millet processing equipment, custom hiring centres, millet value-addition units, and Common Facility Centres (CFCs) where you can pay per use instead of buying.
Status / urgency
Several states (Karnataka, Telangana, AP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Odisha, MP, Uttarakhand, Haryana, Gujarat) run millet-specific schemes. Check your own state first - it is often more generous and easier to get than a central scheme.
How to apply
Contact your District Agriculture Officer / District Industries Centre (DIC) / State Millet Mission cell / State Food Processing department. Ask specifically: (a) is there a millet value-addition unit subsidy, (b) is there a Common Facility Centre within 100 km that I can use for destoning, dehulling, roasting or packing at a per-use charge, (c) is there a state top-up over PMFME.
Fit for you
A COMMON FACILITY CENTRE is the single best capital-saving option for a first-time producer. If one exists near you, you can rent dehusking, roasting, grinding and even packing time for a few rupees per kg instead of buying Rs 3-5 lakh of machines. Do this research in week 1 - it can halve your Phase-1 capex.
Contact / where
Your District Industries Centre (DIC) | District Agriculture Officer | State Millet Mission | statefoodprocessing department website
Udyam Registration (MSME) + MUDRA / Stand-Up India / PMEGP loans
Benefit
Udyam registration is free and unlocks priority-sector lending, lower interest, government tender eligibility and delayed-payment protection. MUDRA gives collateral-free loans up to Rs 20 lakh (Tarun Plus). PMEGP offers 15-35% subsidy on new enterprise projects up to Rs 50 lakh (manufacturing).
Status / urgency
Available year-round. Register on Udyam the same week you register the firm - it is free and takes 20 minutes.
How to apply
Udyam: udyamregistration.gov.in (self-declaration, Aadhaar-based, free). MUDRA/PMEGP: through your bank. Stand-Up India: for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs, Rs 10 lakh - 1 crore.
Fit for you
Udyam is mandatory-in-practice for any MSME. PMEGP can be combined with (or used instead of) PMFME depending on the project - ask your bank which gives you more, and note you generally cannot take two capital subsidies on the same asset.
Contact / where
udyamregistration.gov.in | your bank | kviicportal (PMEGP) | District Industries Centre
FSSAI-related support and FoSCoS
Benefit
FSSAI Basic Registration is Rs 100/year; State Licence Rs 3,000-7,500/year depending on the kind of business. FSSAI also runs free training (FoSTaC) and has a Food Safety Mitra scheme where a certified professional helps small FBOs with compliance for a modest fee.
Status / urgency
*** IMPORTANT REGULATION CHANGE *** FSSAI has revised the turnover thresholds. Per the FoSCoS document updated 01.04.2026: REGISTRATION now covers annual turnover up to Rs 1.5 CRORE (previously Rs 12 lakh); STATE LICENCE covers Rs 1.5 crore to Rs 50 crore; CENTRAL LICENCE above Rs 50 crore (and for importers/exporters and certain other categories). A unit with, say, Rs 1.2 crore turnover that previously needed a State Licence may now remain under Registration. CHECK YOUR CATEGORY ON FoSCoS BEFORE YOU APPLY - applying for the wrong kind of licence wastes months.
How to apply
Apply online at foscos.fssai.gov.in. Download the 'Kind of Business Eligibility' PDF from FoSCoS and find your exact activity (food manufacturing/processing, cereals and cereal products). Upload the required documents and the self-declaration of compliance with Schedule 4 (GHP/GMP). Consider engaging an FSSAI Food Safety Mitra for the first application - it is cheap insurance against a rejected or mis-categorised application.
Fit for you
Mandatory. Budget 2-6 weeks for Basic Registration and 4-10 weeks for a State Licence if required. Do not order machines before you know your premises will pass inspection.
Contact / where
foscos.fssai.gov.in | FSSAI helpline 1800-112-100 | your State Food Safety Commissionerate | a certified FoSTaC trainer or Food Safety Mitra
GST, trademark and other one-time compliance
Benefit
GST registration (mandatory above the threshold, and practically necessary to sell to retailers and e-commerce). Trademark protects your brand name and logo - Rs 4,500 government fee per class for an individual/SME/start-up (Rs 9,000 otherwise), plus professional charges. A registered trademark also lets you use the (R) symbol and is required by most marketplaces.
Status / urgency
File the trademark EARLY - it takes 12-24 months to register and you do not want to launch a brand that someone else already owns. Do a public search on ipindia.gov.in first.
How to apply
GST: gst.gov.in via a CA. Trademark: ipindia.gov.in (you can self-file) or via a trademark attorney. Also register the firm (proprietorship / LLP / Pvt Ltd), get Shop & Establishment registration, and a current bank account.
Fit for you
Do these in week 1-2, before you spend money on packaging artwork that carries a name you cannot protect.
Contact / where
Your CA | ipindia.gov.in | gst.gov.in | a trademark attorney

Quality control and testing plan

Incoming raw material & packaging

What / whenTestsWhere & how longDecision / action
Every lot, every raw materialMoisture, foreign matter, floaters, live insects, mould, odour, colour, lot code, bag conditionIn-house, 15 minReject / accept-with-conditions / reject-immediately gate at S02
Every lot of sprouting-grade ragi/jowar100-grain germination test (36 h)In-house, 36 hBelow 90% (ragi) / 85% (jowar) -> do not use for sprouting
Every lot of kuttuStone check: 500 g hand-picked on a white tray and a 2 mm sieveIn-house, 10 minAny stone -> re-clean; >0.1% -> reject the lot
Every lot of rajgiraSand check: chew/rub a pinch; 40-mesh sieve tailings inspectionIn-house, 5 minGritty -> reject
Every lot of nutsRancidity smell/taste; visual mould; ask for the aflatoxin COAIn-house + COAAny rancidity -> reject the whole lot
Every lot of bought-in flour/powderCOA on file, FSSAI licence number, batch number, best-before, moisture, mesh, sensoryIn-house + paperworkNo COA -> do not use
Per supplier per quarterFull lab panel: heavy metals (Pb, Cd, As), aflatoxin B1, pesticide multi-residue, microbialExternal NABL labAny exceedance -> suspend the supplier
Water (sprouting and cleaning)Potability: microbial (coliform, E. coli), pH, hardness, TDSExternal lab, monthlyNon-potable -> treat before use; stop sprouting
Packaging materialLaminate structure and micron vs the technical data sheet, seal-initiation temperature, WVTR/OTR, food-grade declaration, print accuracyPaperwork + a test sealWrong structure -> return

After cleaning (S03)500 g white-tray check; foreign matter %; magnet inspection; cleaning loss %Every batch

After drying (S05)Moisture every 2 h + at end; snap test; colourEvery batch

Finished product & lab testing

What / whenTestsWhere & how longDecision / action
Every batchMoisture, particle size, sensory (appearance/aroma/texture/taste), weight statistics, seal integrity, label correctness, metal check record, retention samples x3, QA release signatureIn-house, 20-30 min
Every batch of sprouted flour and sprouted mixesFull microbiological panel: TPC, yeast & mould, coliform, E. coli, Salmonella, B. cereusExternal NABL lab - UNTIL you have 12 consecutive clean batches, then move to monthly
MonthlyTPC, yeast & mould, coliform, E. coli on one representative SKU; Salmonella on one sprouted SKUExternal NABL lab
Per SKU, onceFull nutritional analysis for the label panel (energy, protein, carbohydrate, total sugar, fat, saturated fat, trans fat, fibre, sodium) + calcium and iron if you claim themExternal NABL lab, Rs 6,000-12,000 per SKU
QuarterlyHeavy metals (Pb, Cd, As, Hg) and pesticide residues on 2 SKUs on rotation; aflatoxin on any SKU containing nutsExternal NABL lab
Shelf-life validationReal-time at ambient + accelerated at 40 C / 75% RH; assess at 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 270 days: moisture, aw, peroxide value, free fatty acid, TPC/yeast-mould, sensory panelIn-house + external lab
Bajra specificallyPeroxide value and free fatty acid at 0/30/60/90/120 days on every new roast profileExternal lab, Rs 800-2,000 per test
Gluten claim (if you make one)Gluten ELISA (R5) < 20 ppm, per SKU, and after any process changeExternal lab, Rs 3,000-6,000
AnnualRepeat the full panel on 3 SKUs to confirm nothing has driftedExternal lab
Sensory protocol. Train 2-3 people as your sensory panel. Always test in a clean, odour-free area, after stepping outside for 5 minutes (olfactory fatigue is real). Always compare against the RETAINED STANDARD for that SKU, never against memory. Score 1-9 on: colour match, aroma intensity, aroma cleanliness (no rancid/sour/musty/chemical), fineness/grit, and for mixes, the prepared product (drink the malt, cook the dosa). Write down what you detect - 'smells faintly of cardboard' is useful; 'OK' is useless. Any score below 6 on aroma cleanliness = do not release.
Retained standards — make these on day one (under Rs 2,000, removes 90% of operator disagreement). For every SKU keep: (1) a sealed jar of the finished flour at its ideal colour and texture, refreshed every 3 months; (2) a photograph of the ideal roast colour printed and laminated at the roaster; (3) a photograph of a correct seal and an incorrect seal at the sealing station; (4) a photograph of correct label placement at the coding station. These four items cost under Rs 2,000 and they remove 90% of operator disagreement about 'is this good enough?'.

Risk / hazard register (simple HACCP)

IDTypeStageHazardSeverityLikelihoodControlsCritical limitCorrective action
H-01BiologicalS04 SproutingSalmonella / E. coli / Bacillus cereus / Listeria growth during the warm, wet 36-48 h germinationCRITICALMediumPotable (RO/UV) water only, verified monthly; 200 ppm chlorine sanitised tanks and trays every batch, verified with test strips; complete drainage, no pooling; room 25-28 C never >30 C with continuous logging and SMS alarm; 6-8 hourly rinse-turn-drain including nights; dry within 30 min of the stop point; immediate roasting (a kill step) after drying; full micro panel on EVERY batch until 12 consecutive passesRoom <=30 C; sanitiser 200 ppm +-20; to dryer within 30 minAny positive or any spoilage sign: destroy the batch, quarantine adjacent batches, deep-clean and sanitise, test the water, retrain, log an NCR. If any pack was shipped: recall.
H-02BiologicalS02 / S03 / storageMould and mycotoxins (aflatoxin, ochratoxin) from high-moisture or visibly mouldy grainCRITICALMediumReject at intake if moisture >14% or any visible mould/grey-black grains/musty smell; store <=30 C and <=60% RH on pallets with FIFO; buy from approved vendors with a quarterly aflatoxin test; keep the store dry and inspected weeklyMoisture <=12.5% at intake; store RH <=60%Reject the lot. If mould is found in stock, isolate and destroy the affected lot, find the moisture source, and test adjacent stock.
H-03PhysicalS03 / S09Stones, sand and grit from raw grain (kuttu and rajgira are the worst offenders)CRITICALHIGHFour independent layers: (1) destoner-cum-grader-cum-aspirator on every lot, no exceptions; (2) magnet pass at cleaning and again at grinding; (3) correct mesh sieving at S10 with the overs physically inspected every batch; (4) a 30-mesh sieve immediately before filling. Plus hand-picking kuttu on a white tray.Zero stones in a 500 g white-tray check; foreign matter <=0.5%Any stone found downstream: stop, quarantine the batch and the previous batch, 100% re-sieve, investigate the destoner settings and sieve integrity, log an NCR. If packs were shipped, assess a recall.
H-04PhysicalS09 / S10Metal fragments from worn beaters, a holed screen, a broken sieve frame or a toolCRITICALMediumWeekly inspection of beaters, screens and sieve mesh with recorded wear limits; a rare-earth magnetic grate in the chute from day one; no loose tools, no staples, no glass in production; a shadow board with tools counted in and out; Phase 2 metal detector with 2-hourly test-card verificationNo visible metal; magnet finding trace-only; Phase 2: Fe 1.5 / NFe 2.0 / SS 2.5 mm detectedStop, quarantine back to the last good check, identify and photograph the fragment, replace the part, sieve and magnet the quarantined product, log an NCR.
H-05ChemicalS07 / S09 / S18Rancidity / oxidation of high-fat flours (bajra 5-6% fat, rajgira ~7%, kuttu ~3.4%, nuts)HIGHHIGHMandatory roasting to the SKU-specific profile with a recorded temperature-time curve; fast cooling to <=35 C; grind-to-order and pack within 2 h for bajra; foil (AL) laminate pouches - not metallised polyester; 100 cc oxygen absorbers mandatory for bajra, 50 cc for rajgira/sprouted/nut mixes; FG store <=30 C and out of sunlight; honest shelf life (4 months for bajra); PV/FFA testing at 0/30/60/90/120 days on every new profileMoisture <=7% for bajra/rajgira/kuttu; PV and FFA within acceptable limits at the claimed best-before dateUnder-roasted or rancid batch: do not release, do not blend away. Re-roast if the product is still grain; destroy if already ground. Re-validate the profile.
H-06ChemicalS01 / S02Pesticide residues and heavy metals (lead, cadmium, arsenic) in raw grainHIGHLow-MediumApproved vendors with a baseline lab report per grain; a full heavy-metals and pesticide screen per supplier per quarter; buy from known districts rather than anonymous traders; reject any lot that failsFSSAI contaminant limits (Schedule 2 of the Contaminants, Toxins and Residues Regulations)Suspend the supplier; test all stock from that lot; if any finished product is affected, quarantine and assess a recall; notify the Designated Officer.
H-07ChemicalS21 / storesContamination by detergents, sanitisers or pesticidesHIGHLowChemicals in a locked cupboard on an external wall, physically separate from food and packaging; original labelled containers only; a chemical register with MSDS on file; only food-grade detergents and sanitisers inside the plant; a licensed contractor for pesticides with a written chemical list; never spray over or near open product; colour-coded equipmentZero chemical residues on food-contact surfaces (verify by rinse-water check or ATP)If contamination is possible, destroy the affected product. Never 'wash it off and use it'. Retrain, re-lock, re-audit.
H-08Chemical / legalS16Undeclared allergen (groundnut, almond, milk solids) or a wrong ingredient listCRITICALMediumAllergens in RED bins on a red tray, physically separated; nut-free batches run FIRST in the day; a documented full wet-clean after any allergen batch with sign-off before the next batch starts; a flush-bottom blender discharge valve so no dead pocket carries over; bold allergen declaration on EVERY pack including 'may contain' where relevant; second-person verification of every ingredient weight; recipe changes require a re-issued card and a new label versionZero undeclared allergen; label matches formulation exactlyAny suspected undeclared allergen in a shipped pack: immediate recall of that batch, notify the FSSAI Designated Officer, notify every customer who received it the same day. This is never a 'wait and see' situation.
H-09Physical / legalS14Under-weight packs (below the Legal Metrology minimum)MediumMediumDaily scale calibration with certified weights; filler set at declared + 0.4%; 5-pouch check every 30 min; SD <=1%; a stamped legal-for-trade scale; a checkweigher in Phase 2Mean >= declared; no pack below declared - 1.8%Remove and correct short packs; 100% re-weigh the run since the last good check; recalibrate; retrain.
H-10Physical / qualityS14 / S15Moisture ingress and caking from a humid packing room or a failed sealHighHIGHPacking room <=25 C and <=55% RH with a dehumidifier and a logged T-RH; stop filling above 60% RH; foil laminate pouches; a 100% visual seal check plus a squeeze test every 20th pack plus an hourly water/dye test; seal above the zipper and seal the zipper ends; correct film seal-initiation temperature verified against the film's data sheetRH <=55%; 100% seal integrityFailed seals: quarantine back to the last good hourly test, adjust temperature/speed, re-test 5 consecutive packs before resuming, and 100% inspect or re-pack the quarantined stock.
H-11Process / qualityS07Under- or over-roasting from controller drift or variable batch sizeHighMedium-HighIndependent thermometer verification weekly and a full calibration monthly; a grain-bed thermocouple, not a wall one; FIXED batch size per SKU; a retained colour standard jar per SKU; a recorded temperature-time curve per batch; a bite test at the end pointActual vs set temperature within +-5 C; colour matches the standardUnder-roast: continue in 2-min increments. Over-roast: destroy or downgrade the batch (it cannot be blended away), recalibrate, log an NCR.
H-12OperationalAllRecords not filled in, or filled in retrospectivelyHighHIGHLaminated SOP cards at every station with the record attached; a 5-minute daily stand-up; the supervisor signs the batch card before the batch can be released; a weekly record audit; a monthly quality score tied to a small bonus; never allow 'we'll fill it in later'100% of records complete and contemporaneousComplete from contemporaneous notes, identify why the gap happened, retrain. If a batch's records cannot be completed, the batch is not releasable.
H-13Commercial-Launching 10 SKUs at once and running out of money and attentionHighHIGHLaunch 4-5 SKUs. Add the rest on a calendar. Keep finished stock under 30 days. Make small batches often - freshness is your only defensible advantage over unbranded mandi flour.<=30 days of finished stock; <=5 SKUs at launchStop production of slow SKUs and switch to make-to-order. Discount short-dated stock into fast channels before it expires.
H-14Commercial / legalS16Illegal label claims ('cures diabetes', 'baby food', 'organic' without certification, 'gluten free' without testing)Medium-HighMediumHave every artwork checked by a food-regulatory consultant before printing; keep a lab report on file for every nutrition claim; never print an infant or disease claim; use 'naturally gluten-free ingredients' until you have an ELISA test; no 'organic' claim without NPOP/India Organic certificationZero prohibited claims; every claim supported by a report on fileDo not print. If already printed, hold the stock, over-label compliantly where legally possible (never covering MRP or the FSSAI number), and destroy if not.
H-15OperationalS09 / S07 / S05Machine breakdown with no spares and no service engineerMedium-HighMedium-HighKeep the Rs 35,000-70,000 spares kit listed in this pack; buy from vendors with a service engineer within 300 km; own a stone chakki as a backup mill; standardise on universal designs (FR-900 sealer, IS mesh sieves, standard motors); get the AMC price in writing before purchase; keep 2 customer references on file for each vendorAny breakdown resolved within 24 hUse the backup machine; call the vendor; if downtime exceeds 48 h, use a co-packer or a Common Facility Centre to keep orders moving.
H-16Fire / dustS09 / S04Flour dust explosion or fire (fine organic dust is combustible; electric roasters and dryers are ignition sources)CRITICALLowVacuum rather than sweep (never create a dust cloud); keep dust off beams, lights and electrical boxes; no naked flames near dust; proper earthing and bonding of machines; ELCB/RCCB protection; fire extinguishers (CO2 for electrical, ABC for general) mounted and serviced; a roaster/dryer over-temperature cut-out; never leave a roaster or dryer running unattended overnight without a logger alarm; keep aisles clear; a written emergency plan and one drill a yearDust accumulation <1 mm on surfaces; extinguishers in date; ELCB trips on testEvacuate, isolate power, use the correct extinguisher only if safe, call the fire service, and do not re-enter until cleared.
H-17QualityS12Non-uniform blend - a customer gets a pack with no salt, or with a soda hot-spotMediumMediumGeometric dilution for every ingredient below 2%; ordered loading (micro-ingredients last, scattered); 60-75% fill of the blender, never more; a documented cycle; a 5-point uniformity assay with RSD <=5% every batch until 20 consecutive passes; a flush-bottom discharge valveRSD <=5% on the marker assay across 5 pointsRe-blend 5 min and re-test; if still failing, quarantine, investigate the fill level, loading order and ribbon condition, and re-work in two half-batches.
H-18QualityS12 / S14 / S18Particle-size segregation in the dosa mix (coarse settles, fines rise)MediumMedium-HighKeep the particle-size range narrow (no large chunks); a SHORT blend cycle for bimodal mixes (over-blending causes segregation, not mixing); do not drop packs from a height; print 'Shake the pack well before use' prominently; validate with a transport simulationNo visible segregation after a drop and transport testAdjust the grind to narrow the size distribution; shorten the blend; re-test after transport simulation.

Plant layout and material flow

  1. Raw material and finished goods never share a room, a rack, or an air path.
  2. The packing room is entered only through the changing/handwash lobby. No exceptions, including for you.
  3. Wet (sprouting) and dry (packing) areas are separated by a solid wall with self-closing doors.
  4. People flow: changing room -> handwash -> production. Never street clothes into production.
  5. Waste flow: covered bins -> external door -> outside the building. Never carried back through production.
  6. Tool flow: colour-coded and never moved between zones (RED raw/floors, BLUE machines, GREEN packing/food contact, YELLOW sprouting, WHITE QC).
  7. Material flow: forward only. If you find yourself carrying a bag backwards through a door, the layout is wrong.
  8. Every external door: self-closing, close-fitting, with an air curtain or PVC strip curtain, and a rodent guard (a 15 cm metal kick plate).
  9. Every window: meshed. Every light over open product: shatterproof or sleeved.
  10. Floor: epoxy or smooth tile, coved at the wall junction (no 90-degree corners where dirt collects), sloped to a drain in wet areas only.
  11. The sprouting room and the packing room should ideally be at opposite ends of the building.

The daily, weekly and monthly routine

TimeActivityWhat actually happens
07:30Open upSwitch on the dehumidifier in the packing room 60 min BEFORE packing starts. Check and log T-RH in raw store, packing room, FG store. Verify no pest traps have caught anything. Visual walk of the whole plant - look for anything out of place (a spill, an open bag, a tool left out).
07:45Personal hygiene gateEveryone: change into uniform, hairnet, footwear at the door; remove jewellery and phones to the locker; wash and dry hands; the supervisor does a visual check and signs the daily hygiene log.
08:00Machine start-up checksPulveriser: 5-minute pre-run checklist (screen mesh fitted and intact, beaters, gaskets, cyclone, filter bag, magnet, bin clean). Sealer: run 2 empty pouches, tear-test the seal. Filler: verify the scale with the certified weight, run 5 test pouches, record mean and spread. Roaster: preheat and verify temperature with the independent thermometer. Sieves: check mesh. ALL RECORDS SIGNED.
08:15Production meeting (5 minutes)Stand-up at the plan board: what are we making today, in what order, what are the batch codes, who is on which station, what was yesterday's deviation and what are we doing about it. This is the single best management habit you can build.
08:20Batch 1 startsSequence matters. Run the CLEANEST and most allergen-free products FIRST: plain ragi/jowar -> sprouted flours -> mixes without nuts -> mixes with nuts -> oily grains (rajgira, kuttu) LAST. Changeovers follow the cleaning SOP.
10:30Mid-morning QC round5-pouch weight check. Seal squeeze test on the last 20 packs and an hourly water/dye test. Magnet pull and log. Moisture check on the current flour. Roast colour check against the retained standard. Log everything - do not batch up the paperwork to the evening, you will invent it.
11:00Tea breakProduction pauses or a relief operator takes over. No one eats or drinks in production. Hands washed on return.
11:15Production resumesSame checks on restart: 5-pouch weight, seal test, first-pack inspection.
13:00LunchFull stop. Cover or close every open container and bin. Nobody leaves 20 kg of flour open over lunch.
13:45Production resumesRestart checks. Verify nothing was left uncovered.
15:30Afternoon QC roundSame as 10:30. Also: check the FG store T-RH, and reconcile packs produced vs pouches issued vs oxygen absorbers issued - the three numbers must match.
16:30Batch close-outComplete every batch card: weights in, weights out, yields, parameters, deviations, operator and verifier signatures. Move released batches to the FG store and enter them in the FG register THE SAME DAY.
17:00Cleaning (30-45 min)Lock out machines. Brush and VACUUM (never dry-sweep). Wash removable food-contact parts in the 3-sink method. Sanitise (200 ppm chlorine or 70% alcohol). Wipe surfaces, handles, switches. Mop. Empty all waste OUT of the building. Cover or close everything.
17:45Close-down checks and logAll machines off and locked out. Dehumidifier left ON (it runs overnight to protect your stock). Lights off except the pest-control UV units. Doors closed. Cleaning log signed. Tomorrow's plan written on the board. Retention samples put away.
Weekly (Sat)Deep clean + maintenance + reviewStrip-clean all machines per the maintenance schedule. Inspect sieves, screens, beaters, belts, gaskets, Teflon tape. Empty and clean behind machines. Check all pest traps and log counts. Verify all scales and thermometers. Review the week's deviations, yields and complaints with the team (30 min). Plan next week.
MonthlySystem checksCalibrate temperature controllers against an independent thermometer. Descale/verify the moisture analyser. Inspect the water tank and send a water potability sample to the lab. Pest contractor visit and report. Review the complaint log for patterns. Check chemical stock and MSDS file. Audit the record files for completeness.

The 90-day launch plan

WhenWhatDetail and why
Day 1-3Read this whole pack. Then decide your launch SKU subset.Realistic advice: do NOT launch 10 SKUs on day one. Launch 4-5 (Ragi, Jowar, Sprouted Ragi, Malt Mix, Dosa Mix). Add Kuttu and Rajgira in month 2 (they are seasonal and expensive), Bajra in month 3, Sprouted Jowar and Health Mix in month 4. Ten SKUs means ten label artworks, ten lab nutrition panels, ten pouch designs and ten recipes to master. Four means you can actually be excellent.
Day 1-5*** URGENT: chase the PMFME subsidy ***Call your District Resource Person and your bank TODAY. The scheme's stated end date is 30 Sep 2026 (four days away) and an extension has been publicly flagged as likely. Even if it closes, ask about your STATE millet scheme and any Common Facility Centre within 100 km - a CFC can cut your capex by 40-60%.
Day 3-10Legal and registrationFirm registration, PAN, current account, GST, Udyam, trademark search and filing, Shops & Establishments, SPCB consent check. Start these NOW - they take weeks and everything else waits on them.
Day 5-15Premises search and layoutFind 800-1,200 sq ft with three-phase power (or the ability to get it), water, drainage, and a layout that allows one-directional flow. Sketch the zone plan on paper BEFORE signing a lease. A cheap shed with a bad flow will cost you more than an expensive one with a good flow.
Day 10-20Machine RFQs - 3 quotes per machineUse the RFQ template in this pack. Send it to at least: Mill Power/Pulverizer King (Ahmedabad), Nabhitha (Hyderabad), Perfura (Coimbatore), GES Packaging (Faridabad), Axeon (Sangli), and one local fabricator. For every machine demand: SS304 confirmation, a live video demo with YOUR grain, warranty terms in writing, spare-part prices, the name and city of the service engineer, and 2 customer references you can phone.
Day 15-25Raw material sourcingContact 3 suppliers per grain. Buy 1-2 kg samples. Run the germination test on sprouting-grade ragi and jowar. Send baseline samples to an NABL lab. Build the Approved Vendor List. Negotiate terms with a rejection clause.
Day 20-35Fit-outFlooring, partitions, plumbing, electricals, exhaust, insect killers, air curtains, handwash station, changing room, racking. Do this in parallel with machine manufacturing lead time (typically 15-30 days).
Day 25-40Packaging and label designOrder SHORT-RUN digital-print pouches or blank pouches + printed labels (MOQ 500-1,000). Get the label artwork checked by a food-regulatory consultant (Rs 5,000-15,000 per SKU) BEFORE printing 20,000 of them. Get the film technical data sheet (laminate structure, micron, seal-initiation temperature, WVTR/OTR).
Day 30-45FSSAI applicationApply on FoSCoS with the layout plan, machinery list, product list and Schedule 4 self-declaration. Fix anything the inspector flags. Do not order pouches with the licence number printed until you HAVE the number.
Day 35-50Machines arrive - install and commissionDo a formal FAT/SAT: run each machine on your actual grain, measure output kg/h, product temperature, particle size, and power draw. Write it down. Do not pay the final 10-20% until the machine meets the quoted performance - and say so in the purchase order.
Day 45-60Recipe development and trialsThis is the fun part and the part everyone rushes. Run at least 3 trials per SKU. For the mixes: 10 kitchen trials by 10 DIFFERENT households, scored on a written form. Fix the recipes only when the average score is 8.5/10. Record the winning parameters as your master recipe.
Day 50-65Write the SOPs and the batch cardsPrint and laminate a SOP card for every station: the steps, the critical numbers, a photo of GOOD and BAD, and the if/then decision gate. Print the batch cards (R-01 to R-30). Put the cleaning schedule and the pest map on the wall.
Day 55-70Hire and trainHire 4-5 people. Run the 4-hour induction. Certify the three critical stations (sprouting, roasting, packing) by supervised practice - 5 batches each. Do the annual-test paperwork now so the habit exists from day one.
Day 60-75Validation batches + lab testingMake 3 full batches of each launch SKU using the real SOPs and the real people. Send them to the NABL lab: full micro panel on every sprouted SKU, nutrition panels for the label, heavy metals and pesticide screen, and start the shelf-life study (store half at ambient, half at 40 C / 75% RH). Fix whatever the lab or the sensory panel finds. THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT 2 WEEKS IN THE PROJECT.
Day 70-85Shelf-life and packaging validationRun the seal tests (squeeze, water/dye, and a drop test), a 2-week accelerated pack test, and a transport simulation (ship a carton to another city and back, then inspect). Confirm the best-before dates you will print are actually supported.
Day 80-90Mock recall + dry runRun a full mock recall and traceability test. Do a complete production day at 50 kg with all records. Fix the gaps. Photograph everything for your website and your retail pitch deck.
Day 90LAUNCHStart with the 4-5 SKUs, one channel (D2C + 10-20 local kirana/general stores + one quick-commerce listing), and a batch size you can sell in 30 days. Freshness is your only defensible advantage over a Rs 40/kg unbranded mandi flour - protect it by making small batches often.
Month 4-6Add SKUs, then decide on Phase 2Add Bajra (after the shelf-life trial), Kuttu and Rajgira (timed to Navratri), Sprouted Jowar and Health Mix. Only order Phase-2 machines when you are consistently selling more than ~100 kg/day - and add a second shift BEFORE you buy a second line.

Training — turning a layman into an operator

The 4-hour induction

TimeModuleWhat to cover and how
0:00-0:30Who we are, what we make, and why quality mattersShow them the 10 products. Explain that a customer buys millet flour for their child or their diabetic parent - and that one bad pack ends a small brand. Show a real complaint photograph if you have one.
0:30-1:15Personal hygiene and the rules that cannot be brokenHandwash practice (6 steps, actually at the sink). Uniform, hairnet, footwear. No jewellery, no phones, no eating. Blue plaster + glove for any wound. Medical fitness. The visitor log.
1:15-2:00The plant tour and the material flowWalk the whole flow from the intake door to the dispatch door. Show the one-directional principle. Show the colour-coded tools and explain why a red brush never enters the packing room. Show the pest traps and the map.
2:00-2:45Their station's SOP - part 1Read the laminated SOP card for their station together. Explain every number on it and WHY that number exists (people follow rules they understand).
2:45-3:30Their station's SOP - part 2, hands onThey do it while you watch and correct. Then they do it again. Then they do it while explaining it back to you - teaching it back is the only real test of understanding.
3:30-3:50Records: how to fill in a batch cardFill in one real card together. Explain that a record filled in at 6 pm from memory is a fabricated record, and that in an audit an undocumented batch is a failed batch.
3:50-4:00What to do when something goes wrongThe single most important 10 minutes: STOP, do not hide it, tell the supervisor immediately, quarantine the product, and log it. Say explicitly that nobody is ever punished for reporting a problem, and that hiding one is the only thing that gets someone dismissed.
Station certification. For the three critical stations - SPROUTING, ROASTING, and FILLING/SEALING - a person is 'certified' only after they have run 5 consecutive supervised batches with all parameters in specification and all records complete, and the trainer has signed the certification. Until then they work under supervision. Re-certify annually and after any process change.

Twelve monthly toolbox talks

  1. Month 1: Personal hygiene and the handwash audit - watch everyone wash their hands and score it.
  2. Month 2: The roast - colour standards, the bite test, and why under-roasting kills shelf life. Do a blind test with 3 jars.
  3. Month 3: Weights and the law - Legal Metrology, why we set 502 g for a 500 g pack, and what a short pack costs the company.
  4. Month 4: Seals - run a dye test together, deliberately make a bad seal, and let everyone see what a failure looks like.
  5. Month 5: Pest control - walk the plant looking for harborage and food sources; count the traps together.
  6. Month 6: Traceability - pick a random pack off the shelf and have the team trace it back to the grain lot against the clock.
  7. Month 7: Allergens - why nuts go in red bins and why nut-free runs first.
  8. Month 8: Cleaning verification - do a UV-torch inspection of a 'cleaned' machine and show them what they missed.
  9. Month 9: Records and honesty - review a real deviation and how it was handled well.
  10. Month 10: Sprouting food safety - why this one step can make people ill, and the controls.
  11. Month 11: Fire, dust and electrical safety - run the drill.
  12. Month 12: Annual refresher with the 20-question written test (80% pass mark).

The 20-question annual test (80% pass mark)

  1. What is the maximum room RH for packing powder, and what do you do if it is above that?
  2. What is the target fill weight for a 500 g pack, and why is it not exactly 500 g?
  3. What temperature and time does bajra get roasted at, and why is bajra different?
  4. How long may wet sprouted grain wait before it goes into the dryer?
  5. What is the rootlet length at which you stop sprouting ragi, and what happens if you go past it?
  6. How often do you do a squeeze test on seals, and how often a water/dye test?
  7. What do you do if you find a stone in the sifter overs?
  8. What must you do before starting a nut-free batch on the same blender that ran a nut batch?
  9. How often do you pull and inspect the magnet, and what do you do with what you find?
  10. What is the maximum moisture for finished bajra flour, and for a malt mix?
  11. Name three things that must be printed on every pack.
  12. What is the first thing you do if you find a pack that is under-weight?
  13. How often do you verify the scale, and with what?
  14. What do you do if the roaster's controller reads 105 C but your independent thermometer reads 118 C?
  15. What colour is the tool set for the packing room, and why does it matter?
  16. How many retention samples do we keep per batch, and for how long?
  17. What do you do if a batch smells faintly sour?
  18. Who signs the batch release, and what happens if that signature is missing?
  19. What is the first action if you cut your hand?
  20. You drop a tool into the pulveriser and cannot find it. What do you do?
